title: Tig Chambers, Freddie Keppard and the Original Dixieland band
summary: Other New Orleans bands that went north, and how the Original Dixieland band's Livery Stable Blues recording made Dixieland popular.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Another thing, I've seen somebody told me that your brother might have gone up with Tigg Chambers. Do you remember Tigg Chambers ever?

Well, they went up too. They had a band, Tick Chambers, let's see what they had, but they came up after. No one else. No, they came up after that, see. Because all together at one time there was three bands up there from the all-in. Tigg Chambers, Ernest Kelly was playing a trombone I think. I've heard the name of it.
And then another band came back through there, was trumpet played by the name of, what was he, he was a Creole fellow. They had a band because they worked their while too.
Freddie Keffert of course. Well Freddie had been before, she was a show.

They were really the first drill band that went off. But at that time Dixieland wasn't going big. You see, when Dixieland started going big, in the meantime I was in New Orleans, believe it or not, I used to work for Lerocka's uncle. He had a grocery store at the corner of my house.
Well they had the original Dixieland? That's right.

Nick Lerocka. I went a couple of times with them. Then they went to New York, that's when they made the Liberty Stable Blues. You worked with that band? Yeah, I played them a couple of times around there, you know. They didn't think I could play, you know. And that's when they made up their band. They went to New York and made the Liberty Stable Blues and then things busted loose. And that was really telling the truth about it. They wasn't causing Dixieland really getting on top of it like they did. Yeah, they made it popular.
They sure did, they sure did. Yeah, they did. They made these records.
And then Freddie Kepler and them, they had a band all right, but people wasn't paying much attention to Dixieland.
